messages:
maria: Running into a weird issue during onboarding: node quickstart (js-sdk v1.3.0) -> embeddings -> rerank. Some candidate vectors come back length 1023, others 1024. Causes downstream numpy/typedarray reshape errors in the sampleapp.

tony: ouch. which model and which sampleapp tag? any raw http bodies?

maria: model=openembed-medium-2025-04, sampleapp: redwood/quickstart:latest. Repro with the bundled dataset: run `npm run demo:rerank` and you'll hit a ValueError / InvalidTypedArray if you collect into Float32Array(1024).

devon: are both JS and Go SDKs hitting this or just JS?

maria: only saw it in JS so far. I spun up a tiny Go client pointing at the same endpoint and Go always returned 1024-length vectors. Makes me suspect the JS streaming/parsing layer or an autobatcher interaction.

sdk-js: thanks for the report. Two suspects: 1) a streaming retry edge where a partial chunk is concatenated before the second attempt finishes, 2) the response field name change we rolled out earlier this month. We renamed `vector` -> `embedding` on some routes; older SDK parse paths look for `vector` and fallback code can accidentally concat different fields.

maria: here's a sanitized raw response (from REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1):
```json
{"candidates": [{"id":"a1","vector":[0.12,...,<1023 floats>]},{"id":"a2","embedding":[<1024 floats>]}]}
```
that mixed `vector` and `embedding` in same body.

tony: mixed field names inside one response definitely smells like gateway/migration mismatch. Server should be consistent. Do you have the full request-id header? that helps route to the right backend.

maria: x-request-id: rwd-req-2026-zz123. Attached logs: https://redwood-internal/snapshots/1769991122.

sdk-js: OK we'll trace. In the short term: workaround is to normalize both fields after parse: prefer `embedding` if present, else `vector`. Also disable autobatching: `client.rerank.batch(..., autobatch: false)` or set `REDWOOD_AUTOBATCH=false` in env for the sampleapp.

devon: can we add a safe guard in the JS SDK to assert all candidate embeddings have the same length and throw a descriptive error if not? New users hitting this during quickstart will be confused.

sdk-js: yes, adding an assertion before any reshape/typedarray allocation. We'll also add a debug log that prints lengths per-candidate and the request-id. Also opening PR to make the parse code accept both `vector` and `embedding` in the same response but normalized in-memory.

sdk-go: FYI we already added the normalization in Go last quarter which prevented this class of failure there. Aligning JS with Go makes sense.

ciara-bot: incident created: INC-2026-324 embed-field-migration-mix (priority: medium)

tony: product note: quickstart sampleapp should pin a compatible SDK and include a troubleshooting step: "If you see inconsistent vector lengths, set REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1 and try autobatch=false."

maria: confirmed workaround works (autobatch off + normalization). Demo unblocked. thanks! :party-parrot:

sdk-js: timeline: hotfix for assertion + normalization will land in v1.3.1 today, sampleapp update tomorrow to pin v1.3.1. We'll also add a migration guard on the gateway so responses are consistent.

devon: follow-up: add an e2e test that exercises the streaming retry + field-name combos (vector vs embedding) so this doesn't regress.

sdk-js: added to test plan. will post PRs and release notes here.
